Interface Backend

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractBackend, AeshBackend, JLineBackend, PanamaBackend, RecordingBackend
public interface Backend extends AutoCloseable
Backend interface for terminal operations. Implementations handle the actual terminal I/O.

  • Method Details

    • draw

      void draw(DiffResult diff) throws IOException
      Draws the given cell updates to the terminal using a Data-Oriented Design approach.

      This is the primary rendering method, optimized for zero allocations with parallel arrays.

      Parameters:
      diff - the diff result containing cell updates in Structure-of-Arrays format
      Throws:
      IOException - if drawing fails
      See Also:
      • AbstractBackend
      • DiffResult

    • enableBracketedPaste

      default void enableBracketedPaste() throws IOException
      Enables bracketed paste mode (ESC[?2004h).

      When active, pasted text is wrapped with ESC[200~ / ESC[201~ markers so the event parser can deliver the full paste as a single PasteEvent instead of individual key events.

      Throws:
      IOException - if writing to the terminal fails

    • disableBracketedPaste

      default void disableBracketedPaste() throws IOException
      Disables bracketed paste mode (ESC[?2004l).
      Throws:
      IOException - if writing to the terminal fails

    • writeRaw

      default void writeRaw(byte[] data) throws IOException
      Writes raw bytes directly to the terminal output.

      This is used for native image protocols (Sixel, Kitty, iTerm2) that require sending escape sequences with binary data.

      Parameters:
      data - the raw bytes to write
      Throws:
      IOException - if writing fails

    • writeRaw

      default void writeRaw(String data) throws IOException
      Writes a raw string directly to the terminal output.

      This is a convenience method for protocols that work with ASCII escape sequences.

      Parameters:
      data - the string to write
      Throws:
      IOException - if writing fails

    • writeRaw
